items.stem: In 1937, when the Supreme Court struck down several key New Deal programs as unconstitutional, FDR proposed his 'court-packing' plan to add up to six new justices. The plan was ultimately rejected — even by many congressional Democrats. Which analysis BEST explains why even FDR's political allies opposed the court-packing plan?
items.stemEs: En 1937, cuando la Corte Suprema anuló varios programas clave del New Deal como inconstitucionales, FDR propuso su plan de 'empaquetamiento del tribunal' para agregar hasta seis nuevos jueces. El plan fue finalmente rechazado, incluso por muchos demócratas del Congreso. ¿Qué análisis explica MEJOR por qué incluso los aliados políticos de FDR se opusieron al plan de empaquetamiento del tribunal?

choices.text: Even New Deal supporters recognized that manipulating court composition to ensure favorable rulings would undermine judicial independence as a structural protection for all future governments — a precedent they were unwilling to set regardless of their policy preferences.
choices.textEs: Incluso los partidarios del New Deal reconocieron que manipular la composición del tribunal para garantizar fallos favorables socavaría la independencia judicial como protección estructural para todos los gobiernos futuros, un precedente que no estaban dispuestos a establecer independientemente de sus preferencias políticas.

choices.text: Democrats opposed the plan because they feared that adding justices would increase the federal judiciary's workload, requiring additional funding that would undermine New Deal spending priorities.
choices.textEs: Los demócratas se opusieron al plan porque temían que agregar jueces aumentaría la carga de trabajo de la judicatura federal, requiriendo fondos adicionales que socavarían las prioridades de gasto del New Deal.

choices.text: Congressional Democrats opposed the plan because they believed the Supreme Court's rulings against New Deal programs were correct on constitutional grounds, and that FDR should instead write legislation that complied with the Constitution.
choices.textEs: Los demócratas del Congreso se opusieron al plan porque creían que los fallos de la Corte Suprema contra los programas del New Deal eran correctos desde el punto de vista constitucional, y que FDR debería en cambio redactar legislación que cumpliera con la Constitución.

choices.text: Democrats in Congress opposed court-packing because FDR had not consulted them before announcing the plan, and the lack of consultation was seen as an executive overreach that threatened the independence of the legislative branch.
choices.textEs: Los demócratas en el Congreso se opusieron al empaquetamiento del tribunal porque FDR no los había consultado antes de anunciar el plan, y la falta de consulta fue vista como un exceso ejecutivo que amenazaba la independencia del poder legislativo.

items.stem: The Truman Doctrine (1947) pledged American support for free peoples resisting subjugation, while the Marshall Plan (1947) committed roughly $13 billion to European economic reconstruction. How do these two initiatives together reflect a coherent and unified strategic logic for containing Soviet influence in postwar Europe?

choices.text: The Truman Doctrine and Marshall Plan were complementary primarily through their combined military and security dimensions — both relied on American military guarantees to deter Soviet armed aggression, with economic aid functioning as a secondary incentive to maintain Western-aligned governments.

The Truman Doctrine established a global ideological framework for containment, but the Marshall Plan was primarily motivated by American economic self-interest in creating prosperous European export markets — suggesting that strategic and commercial interests happened to align in this case rather than reflecting a single coherent anti-Soviet vision.

The two initiatives reflected the strategic insight that communism thrived in conditions of economic desperation and political instability — military containment alone would be insufficient if poverty created conditions in which Soviet-backed political movements could gain genuine popular support, making economic reconstruction a strategic necessity rather than purely humanitarian charity.

Truman and Marshall designed their respective programs as deliberate provocations intended to force the Soviet Union into an unsustainable military competition, representing early applications of the rollback strategy later associated with Eisenhower's New Look defense policy.

items.stem: The Civil Rights Act of 1964 prohibited racial discrimination in public accommodations, employment, and federally funded programs. Given that many Southern states had maintained legally enforced segregation for nearly a century after the Fourteenth Amendment's passage, what does the Act's eventual passage most reveal about the conditions required for transformative civil rights legislation?
items.stemEs: La Ley de Derechos Civiles de 1964 prohibió la discriminación racial en los establecimientos públicos, el empleo y los programas financiados con fondos federales. Dado que muchos estados del Sur habían mantenido una segregación legalmente impuesta durante casi un siglo después de la aprobación de la Decimocuarta Enmienda, ¿qué revela más claramente la eventual aprobación de la Ley sobre las condiciones necesarias para la legislación transformadora en materia de derechos civiles?

choices.text: The Act's passage required the convergence of sustained grassroots mobilization that disrupted segregation's daily functioning, television coverage that made white violence against nonviolent protesters politically costly to tolerate, and presidential leadership committed to legislative action — demonstrating that transformative civil rights legislation emerges from the alignment of movement pressure, public opinion shifts, and executive political
choices.textEs: La aprobación de la Ley requirió la convergencia de una movilización popular sostenida que perturbó el funcionamiento diario de la segregación, la cobertura televisiva que hizo políticamente costoso tolerar la violencia blanca contra los manifestantes no violentos, y el liderazgo presidencial comprometido con la acción legislativa —demostrando que la legislación transformadora de derechos civiles surge de la alineación de la presión del movimiento, los cambios en la opinión pública y la voluntad política ejecutiva.

choices.text: The Act's passage shows that economic modernization in the South had eroded the material foundation of segregation by creating a business class that recognized international competitiveness required abandoning racial discrimination, making economic development the primary structural driver of civil rights legislation.
choices.textEs: La aprobación de la Ley muestra que la modernización económica del Sur había erosionado la base material de la segregación al crear una clase empresarial que reconoció que la competitividad internacional requería abandonar la discriminación racial, haciendo del desarrollo económico el principal motor estructural de la legislación de derechos civiles.

choices.text: The Act demonstrated that moral argument alone can overcome entrenched racial hierarchies, as the movement's nonviolent discipline and the moral clarity of its witness ultimately convinced a sufficient congressional majority to act despite fierce Southern opposition.
choices.textEs: La Ley demostró que el argumento moral por sí solo puede superar las jerarquías raciales arraigadas, ya que la disciplina no violenta del movimiento y la claridad moral de su testimonio finalmente convencieron a una mayoría suficiente del Congreso de actuar a pesar de la feroz oposición del Sur.

choices.text: The Civil Rights Act passed primarily because of Lyndon Johnson's legislative mastery and his exploitation of the national emotional response to Kennedy's assassination, suggesting that individual political leadership and historically contingent events were more decisive than structural conditions in producing the legislation.
choices.textEs: La Ley de Derechos Civiles se aprobó principalmente gracias al dominio legislativo de Lyndon Johnson y su explotación de la respuesta emocional nacional al asesinato de Kennedy, lo que sugiere que el liderazgo político individual y los eventos históricamente contingentes fueron más decisivos que las condiciones estructurales para producir la legislación.
